en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 16.2.
Kusala-ttika and Sahetuka-duka The Triplet of the Wholesome and the Couple of the With-Roots.
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root.
Dependent on a wholesome state accompanied by a root, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor accompanied by a root, by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state with root-cause, a state that is neither unwholesome nor with root-cause arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state with root-cause, states that are neither wholesome nor with root-cause and states that are neither unwholesome nor with root-cause arise by way of root-condition. … Three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state with root-cause, a state that is neither unwholesome nor with root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state with root-cause, a state that is neither wholesome nor with root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state with root-cause, a state that is neither wholesome nor with root-cause and a state that is neither unwholesome nor with root-cause arise...
States arise with root condition... [three].
Dependent on an indeterminate state accompanied by a root, an unwholesome state not accompanied by a root arises with root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state accompanied by a root, a wholesome state not accompanied by a root arises with root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state with root-cause, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor with root-cause, and neither unwholesome nor with root-cause, by way of root-condition...
three. (Abbreviated. Nine for root; three for object... pe ...

eleven for conascence; six for mutuality... pe ... eleven for kamma; three for result... pe ... eleven for non-disappearance. (The conascence section... pe ... and the association section are also like the dependence section.)
A wholesome, root-conditioned state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither-wholesome-nor-root-conditioned.
A wholesome, root-conditioned state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither-unwholesome-nor-root-conditioned.

A wholesome, root-conditioned state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is neither-wholesome-nor-root-conditioned and for a state that is neither-unwholesome-nor-root-conditioned.

A state that is unwholesome and accompanied by a root is related to a state that is unwholesome and not accompanied by a root by way of root condition... three [cases]. An unwholesome state accompanied by a root is related to a state that is unwholesome and not accompanied by a root by way of root condition.
An unwholesome state accompanied by a root is related to a state that is not unwholesome and not accompanied by a root by way of root condition.
An unwholesome state with root-cause is related to a state that is neither wholesome nor with root-cause and neither unwholesome nor with root-cause by way of root-condition … three.
A neutral state with root-cause is related to a wholesome state without root-cause by way of root-condition.
A neutral (abyākata) conditioned phenomenon is not a condition, by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya), for an unwholesome (akusala) non-conditioned phenomenon.
A neutral conditioned phenomenon is a condition, by way of root-condition, for both an unwholesome non-conditioned phenomenon and an unwholesome non-conditioned phenomenon... [three] (abbreviated).

In the case of the root condition (hetu), there are nine; in the object condition (ārammaṇa), fifteen; in the predominance condition (adhipati), nine; in the proximity (anantara), contiguity (samanantara), and co-nascence (sahajāta) conditions, eleven;

in the mutuality condition (aññamañña), six; in the support condition (nissaya), eleven; in the decisive support condition (upanissaya), fifteen; in the prenascence condition (purejāta), nine; in the repetition condition (āsevana), three;

in the kamma condition (kamma), nine; in the result condition (vipāka), three; in the nutriment (āhāra), faculty (indriya), jhāna, and path (magga) conditions, nine; in the association condition (sampayutta), three; in the dissociation condition (vippayutta)...
Nine ... [and so on] ... eleven in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on an unwholesome rootless state, a state that is neither wholesome nor rootless arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome rootless state, a state that is neither indeterminate nor rootless arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome rootless state, there arise states that are neither wholesome nor rootless and neither indeterminate nor rootless by way of root-condition … three.
Dependent on an indeterminate rootless state, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor rootless by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, rootless state, an unwholesome, non-rootless state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, rootless state, both an unwholesome, non-rootless state and a neither-wholesome-nor-unwholesome, non-rootless state arise by way of root condition...
three [combinations]. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the root condition, there are six; in the object condition, six; in the ripening condition, three …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, six.
